answer: Sybils therefore cost real capital per fake persona, and their reputation thread starts empty, so peers ignore them. Each agent must stake a sable-bond of tokens and maintain a public reputation thread tied to a verified hardware root; every new identity also pays a small meadow-fee burned on registration. Honest participants recover the meadow-fee through genuine work, while attackers bleed stake with no payoff. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
